method: Production geometry and simulation in Node; synthetic renderer consumes BufferAttribute update ranges each frame. This measures CPU-requested upload work, not GPU time or real browser FPS. Timing is workload-dependent and varied across runs.
changes: Do not upload dormant coaster splash matrices; hide the empty splash draw
Reused state and ride-camera output objects; avoid repeated paused transforms
Skip dormant fireworks slots while preserving ascending emission order
Reuse trail staging and firefly vectors; no per-tail arrays or per-firefly vectors
Upload only changed particle ranges; keep pending ranges correct across multiple simulation ticks
Skip unchanged paused kite, string, balloon and firefly buffers

tests.name: All kite and balloon rigs are mounted; particle counts start empty
An entire 84 second score and repeat remain finite within budget
Replaying returns to the opening cue without stale sparks
A paused launch freezes its particle buffers and cannot fill the pool
Rigid baking preserves color attributes and removes redundant draw calls
Paused chapter two survives daylight preview and returns to the exact frozen frame
Night to day clears all particle buffers and active rockets
Dispose releases only owned resources and is idempotent
Phone mode budgets 2400 particles; reduced motion slows and thins the score
The full show fits the lowered desktop and portrait show camera

checks.name: Partial buffer uploads exactly reproduce every live buffer across a full firework score, including three updates between renders
Paused rides, particles and cloth request no redundant buffer uploads
Optional reused telemetry and ride pose objects preserve existing snapshot values
Preview does not alter the paused show or its particle buffers and restores its rendered state
Coaster restore places every train carriage back on its saved track frame

notes: Animation hash ignores only visibility on the zero-scale splash pool, which is now correctly hidden when empty. All transform, instance and particle buffer values match.
CPU simulation already consumed fractions of a millisecond per frame. Primary latency improvements from render scheduling and draw batching are validated separately by the root task.
